<a id="demolockpolicy"></a>

## `DemoLockPolicy`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.DemoLockPolicy` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

RP-2. The loader runs on the full Steam release of Chill With You: Lo-Fi Story only, never on the free demo. The demo is a separate Steam app whose build sets `BulbulConstant.IsDemo`; any one piece of evidence that this is not the full game locks the loader. Facts that could not be read never lock on their own, so a game update that moves a constant cannot switch the loader off for paying players: the version gate and the patch-target report cover that case.

<a id="demolockpolicy--fullgameappid"></a>

### `const uint FullGameAppId = 3548580`

Steam app id of the full game (store page app/3548580).

<a id="demolockpolicy--playermessage"></a>

### `const string PlayerMessage = "CWY:LS Mod Loader only runs on the full game. This looks like the demo, so the loader and every mod are switched off and the game runs as normal. Get the full game on Steam to use mods."`

Shown on screen and logged when the lock engages.

<a id="demolockpolicy--testswitch"></a>

### `const string TestSwitch = "CWYLS_DEMO_LOCK_TEST"`

Environment variable that forces the lock on for testing (`CWYLS_DEMO_LOCK_TEST=1`). There is deliberately no switch the other way.

<a id="demolockpolicy--evaluate"></a>

### `static DemoLockVerdict Evaluate(DemoLockFacts facts)`

Decides whether the loader may run.

**Parameters**

- `facts`: What could be read at startup; null is treated as "nothing read".

<a id="demolockpolicy--mentionsdemo"></a>

### `static bool MentionsDemo(string text)`

True when `text` contains "demo" as a word of its own (any case): "Chill with You Lo-Fi Story Demo" and "Demo\_Data" count, "Demonstration" does not.

<a id="gameversiongate"></a>

## `GameVersionGate`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.GameVersionGate` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Compares the running game's version against the build the patch-target tables describe, for the framework itself. A mismatch never aborts anything: the patch-target report is the real evidence, and this gate only explains *why* a target might have moved.

Content packs are not gated by this class. Their `gameVersion`, `minGameVersion` and `maxGameVersion` follow [`PackGameVersionCheck`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#packgameversioncheck).

Versions compare by SemVer precedence where both sides parse ([`GameVersions.TryParse`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#gameversions--tryparse)), so build metadata such as `1.17.2+steam.1` matches `1.17.2`; otherwise by exact text.

Creates a gate for [`GameVersionGate.ExpectedGameVersion`](#gameversiongate--expectedgameversion).

<a id="gameversiongate--ctor-string"></a>

Creates a gate for an explicit expected version (used by tests).

**Parameters**

- `expected`: The version the targets were verified against.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `expected` is null or blank.

<a id="gameversiongate--expectedgameversion"></a>

<a id="gameversiongate--unknownversion"></a>

<a id="gameversiongate--expected"></a>

### `string Expected { get; }`

<a id="gameversiongate--check"></a>

### `GameVersionCheck Check(string actual)`

Compares a reported version against [`GameVersionGate.Expected`](#gameversiongate--expected).

**Parameters**

- `actual`: The running game's version, normally `UnityEngine.Application.version`. Null or blank is reported as a mismatch, not silently accepted.

<a id="minijson"></a>

## `MiniJson`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.MiniJson` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

A deliberately tiny JSON *writer*. The plugins run on Unity's Mono profile where System.Text.Json does not exist; Newtonsoft.Json ships with the game, but pulling a game assembly in just to emit a status file would tie this logic to the game install and make it untestable off-Unity. Writing a few dozen bytes of JSON by hand is cheaper than either.

Reading is the other half and lives in [`JsonReader`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Json.md#jsonreader) - also written here rather than borrowed from the game, for the same reason: nothing in Core may need Unity or the game install to be unit-tested. Pack manifests are parsed by that reader, not by Newtonsoft.

<a id="patchsignature"></a>

## `PatchSignature`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.PatchSignature` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Builds the canonical signature strings used by [`PatchTarget.ExpectedSignature`](#patchtarget--expectedsignature) and by resolver results, e.g. `UniTask Load()` or `static int Count`. The canonical form deliberately drops namespaces and uses C# keyword aliases, so a target table reads the way the game's members are written in C#. Both sides of a comparison go through this class, so "expected" and "actual" are always normalised identically.

<a id="patchsignature--unknowntype"></a>

### `const string UnknownType = "?"`

Rendered in place of a type name that could not be determined.

<a id="patchsignature--forfield"></a>

### `static string ForField(string fieldTypeName, string memberName, bool isStatic)`

Canonical form of a field: `[static ]<type> <name>`.

**Parameters**

- `fieldTypeName`: Field type name; shortened by [`PatchSignature.ShortName`](#patchsignature--shortname).
- `memberName`: Field name.
- `isStatic`: Whether the field is static (enum constants are).

<a id="patchsignature--formethod"></a>

### `static string ForMethod(string returnTypeName, string memberName, IEnumerable<string> parameterTypeNames, bool isStatic)`

Canonical form of a method: `[static ]<return> <name>(<params>)`.

**Parameters**

- `returnTypeName`: Return type name; shortened by [`PatchSignature.ShortName`](#patchsignature--shortname).
- `memberName`: Method name.
- `parameterTypeNames`: Parameter type names in declaration order; may be empty.
- `isStatic`: Whether the method is static.

<a id="patchsignature--forproperty"></a>

### `static string ForProperty(string propertyTypeName, string memberName, bool canRead, bool canWrite, bool isStatic)`

Canonical form of a property: `[static ]<type> <name> { get; set; }`, with only the accessors that actually exist.

**Parameters**

- `propertyTypeName`: Property type name; shortened by [`PatchSignature.ShortName`](#patchsignature--shortname).
- `memberName`: Property name.
- `canRead`: Whether the property has a getter.
- `canWrite`: Whether the property has a setter.
- `isStatic`: Whether the property's accessors are static.

<a id="patchsignature--shortname"></a>

### `static string ShortName(string typeName)`

Shortens a type name for display: `System.Int32` becomes `int`, `Bulbul.HeroineService+AnimationType` becomes `HeroineService.AnimationType`, and every identifier inside a generic argument list is shortened the same way, so `R3.Observable<R3.Unit>` becomes `Observable<Unit>`.

The input must be a *reflection* type name, where nesting is written with `+`. A dotted prefix is always read as a namespace, so this is not idempotent over its own output for a nested type - `HeroineService.AnimationType` would shorten again to `AnimationType`. Nothing calls it twice: signatures are built once from reflection and then compared as plain strings.

**Parameters**

- `typeName`: A reflection type name, possibly with generic arguments in angle brackets.

<a id="patchtarget"></a>

## `PatchTarget`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.PatchTarget` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

One member of the game the framework relies on: the executable form of one verified seam. A target is pure data - assembly, type and member names as strings - so the table can name members of assemblies this project does not reference at compile time, and so it can be unit-tested without Unity.

<a id="patchtarget--ctor"></a>

### `PatchTarget(string id, string assembly, string typeName, MemberKind memberKind, string memberName, string[] parameterTypeNames = null, bool isStatic = false, string expectedSignature = null)`

Creates a target.

**Parameters**

- `id`: Stable, unique, lower-case dotted id used in log lines, e.g. `heroine.playvoice`.
- `assembly`: Simple assembly name, e.g. `Assembly-CSharp`.
- `typeName`: Reflection type name, e.g. `Bulbul.HeroineService`, `HeroineAI+ActionStateType` for a nested type, or `` KanKikuchi.AudioManager.AudioManager`1 `` for a generic definition.
- `memberKind`: Method, field or property.
- `memberName`: Member name, private members included.
- `parameterTypeNames`: Full parameter type names in declaration order, for [`MemberKind.Method`](#memberkind--method) only. An empty or null list means *the method takes no parameters* - it is not a wildcard.
- `isStatic`: Whether the member is static.
- `expectedSignature`: Optional canonical signature (see [`PatchSignature`](#patchsignature)), e.g. `UniTask Load()`. When set, a resolver that finds the member but reads a different signature reports the target as missing, because the seam is no longer the shape the framework was written against.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: A required name is null or blank, or a non-method target was given parameter types.

Simple name of the assembly that must declare the type.

Canonical signature the framework was written against, or null if unchecked.

### `string Id { get; }`

<a id="patchtarget--isstatic"></a>

### `bool IsStatic { get; }`

Whether the member is static.

<a id="patchtargetchecker"></a>

## `PatchTargetChecker`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.PatchTargetChecker` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Runs a patch-target table through a resolver and collects a [`PatchTargetReport`](#patchtargetreport).

<a id="patchtargetchecker--check"></a>

### `static PatchTargetReport Check(IEnumerable<PatchTarget> targets, IMemberResolver resolver)`

Checks every target. A resolver that throws is treated as a missing target rather than being allowed to abort the sweep: one broken seam must not hide the other twenty-five. The exception text lands in [`PatchTargetResult.Detail`](#patchtargetresult--detail), which the plugin-side verifier logs at Error - this layer has no logger of its own by design (no BepInEx here).

**Parameters**

- `targets`: The table to check.
- `resolver`: How to look each target up.

**Returns:** A report over all targets, in table order.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `targets` or `resolver` is null.
